content_of_post_to_answer: Is it normal to be forgetful when under great emotional stress?
answer: Stress-related forgetfulness is often misunderstood as a failure of memory when it is usually a failure of attention. When the brain is occupied with threat, grief, anxiety, or emotional overload, it has fewer resources available to encode ordinary details. A person may not be losing memories; they may never have fully stored them. The overlooked distinction is that a stressed mind often forgets what it couldn't safely prioritize in the first place.
